reason: Non-material. The root cause, trace (every path and line rechecked at 3586750), execution input, observed result, impact and severity all stand, and the Phase 5 sandbox rerun reproduced the result (1,000,001 cell.text calls at gridSpan 1e6, 476.2 MiB, 22.4 s against a 1 s limit). Corrected: (1) remediation code_changes. The original fixed_code called self._docx.table._Cell, but _Writer has no _docx attribute and docx.py imports python-docx lazily. Run in the sandbox, it turned every docx table into a 'failed' AttributeError render. The replacement passes the cell class in from render(), and it keeps vMerge='continue' text by reusing the cell above. Executed, it renders the 1e6 input 'ok' with 1 cell.text call, and on a merged 3x3 table its output is identical to the current renderer. (2) Wording: the input was 36,703 to 36,705 bytes, not a constant 36,705. (3) Two new evidence entries cite this rerun.

record.title: A docx table cell's gridSpan value expands into an unbounded cell list before any render limit applies
record.description: _Writer.table builds rows = [[cell.text for cell in row.cells] for row in table.rows] and only then hands the rows to Builder.table. In the installed python-docx 1.2.0, _Row.cells yields the same _Cell once for each grid column the cell spans (iter_tc_cells: for _ in range(tc.grid_span): yield cell). grid_span is read straight from the w:tcPr/w:gridSpan/@val integer and is never compared with the table's real grid width. The renderer then calls cell.text once for each yielded entry, and each call builds a new string. So one attribute in a document of about 36 KB decides how many tuple entries, cell.text calls and list strings get created. All of this work finishes before Builder sees the first row. The character budget, the ratio guard, the unit cap and the cooperative clock (RenderLimits.seconds, checked only at block boundaries and between table rows) therefore do not bound it. The bytes come from any principal allowed to write(data=...) to a DatabaseStorage mount; the write stores them as render_status='pending'. The expansion runs later, when the operator calls reindex(). It runs on the backend's in-process ThreadPoolExecutor, the pool that grep's verify stage also uses, and a running worker cannot be interrupted. Local run: input size held constant at about 36.7 KB (36,703 to 36,705 bytes), gridSpan raised from 1e3 to 1e6. cell.text calls grew exactly linearly (1,000 to 1,000,000). Peak RSS rose from 113.6 MiB to 473.0 MiB. Wall time was about 22 s against RenderLimits(seconds=1.0); this is informational only. Spans of 1e5 and above also return status 'empty' with no text, because the header line alone overflows the character budget. Correction to the hunter's wording: a render that completes lands a terminal state and is not retried. A row stays pending, and is retried on every reindex, only when the span is large enough that the render never finishes or the process dies. The schema allows values up to 2^31-1. That size was not executed: by extrapolation it is more than 16 GiB of tuple pointers alone, plus hours of CPU.
record.root_cause: DocxRenderer's table path builds the span-expanded row.cells tuple and one cell.text string per grid position, with no cap and no clamp to the table's declared grid width. RenderLimits are enforced only inside Builder, on text it emits. The materialization runs as one uninterruptible step on the offload thread, before any of those checks.
record.intended_behavior: A render's memory and CPU should stay bounded by RenderLimits and roughly proportional to the input bytes. Per the seam's own docstring, a malformed or hostile docx should end as a classified 'truncated' or 'failed' state within the time budget, not do work set by an attribute value.

trace.description: A lower-trust caller with write rights stores arbitrary docx bytes through write(data=...)
The bytes row is stored with render_status='pending' and is not rendered in the writer's call
The operator's reindex() renders every pending bytes row via render_rows on the in-process offload ThreadPoolExecutor (call_offloaded)
Each pending row goes to registry.render with the configured RenderLimits
Dispatches to DocxRenderer.render; only an Exception raised from inside the renderer becomes a state
Each body table block goes to _Writer.table after a single boundary() clock check

rows = [[cell.text for cell in row.cells] for row in table.rows] creates one tuple entry and one cell.text string per spanned grid column, with the count set by w:gridSpan/@val, before Builder.table checks any budget

evidence.description: The full row matrix is materialized before self._builder.table(rows) runs; there is no cap on len(row.cells) and no clamp to the table grid
Builder.table checks out_of_time() and the character budget only while emitting rows that already exist
RenderLimits caps characters, ratio, embedded objects, units and seconds; none of these bounds parsed structure size or work done before Builder
The offload pool is an in-process ThreadPoolExecutor shared with grep's verify stage, so memory and CPU exhaustion affects the whole host process

Sandboxed run, constant 36,703 to 36,705-byte input: gridSpan 1e3/1e4/1e5/1e6 gives cell.text calls of exactly 1e3/1e4/1e5/1e6 and peak RSS of 113.6/117.2/148.6/473.0 MiB; wall time 22.4 s at 1e6 against a 1.0 s limit

The harness: builds a 1x1 docx with python-docx, sets w:gridSpan/@val, counts _Cell.text calls, and calls RendererRegistry.bundled().render(RenderSource(data, DOCX, 'a.docx'), RenderLimits(seconds=1.0))
Independent Phase 5 sandbox rerun at gridSpan 1e6 on a 36,718-byte input: 1,000,001 cell.text calls, status 'empty', peak RSS 476.2 MiB, wall 22.4 s (informational) against RenderLimits(seconds=1.0)

The corrected remediation, patched in under the sandbox: the same gridSpan 1e6 input renders 'ok' with 1 cell.text call; on a 3x3 table with a horizontal and a vertical merge it emits text identical to the current renderer

conditions.description: The attacker can write bytes entries to a DatabaseStorage mount (any subject with write rights on some path)
The vfs[docx] extra (python-docx) is installed, so the docx renderer is available
The operator or host later runs DatabaseStorage.reindex(), the only place rendering happens
python-docx 1.2.0 _Row.cells expands a horizontal span into grid_span repeated cells, taken from the unvalidated w:gridSpan/@val

execution.attacker_perspective: A lower-trust agent or ETL writer with ordinary write rights stores one small .docx entry. The renderer cost lands later on the operator's reindex, in the host process that all agents share.
payloads: A word/document.xml holding one table, one w:tc whose w:tcPr contains <w:gridSpan w:val="1000000"/> and a paragraph of 100 characters (about 36 KB zipped)
instructions: Build a 1x1 table docx with python-docx, put 100 characters in the cell, and append w:gridSpan with w:val=N to the cell's w:tcPr
Call RendererRegistry.bundled().render(RenderSource(data, DOCX, 'a.docx'), RenderLimits(seconds=1.0)) in the sandbox, counting _Cell.text calls and reading ru_maxrss
Repeat for N = 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 with the input size held constant, and stop there (no larger values)
execution.observed_result: Input stayed at 36,703 to 36,705 bytes. cell.text calls equalled N exactly (1,000 to 1,000,000). Peak RSS grew from 113.6 MiB to 473.0 MiB. Wall time at N=1e6 was 22.4 s against RenderLimits.seconds=1.0, so the clock did not stop the expansion. Statuses were 'ok' for 1e3 and 1e4, and 'empty' ('no text in 1 units') for 1e5 and 1e6. Work and memory grow linearly with the attribute value, not with the input size. An independent Phase 5 rerun (two-row table, the same 100-character cell) reproduced it: 1,000,001 cell.text calls, status 'empty', peak RSS 476.2 MiB, 22.4 s against seconds=1.0.

remediation.strategy: Do not iterate python-docx's span-expanded row.cells. Walk each row's w:tc elements directly. Compute each cell's text once. Clamp each span to the table's declared grid width (len(tblGrid.gridCol_lst), which is proportional to the parsed input) and to the columns that remain in the row. Then repeat the already computed string, so the row length is bounded by the grid actually present. For a vMerge='continue' cell, reuse the text already collected at the same grid position in the row above, which keeps python-docx's current output without its recursive walk. docx.py imports python-docx lazily (DocxRenderer.library), so the cell class must be handed to _Writer from render(); the record's earlier fixed_code referenced a nonexistent self._docx and, when run, turned every docx table into a 'failed' render with AttributeError. Optionally check builder.out_of_time() between rows during collection; the builder already remembers the timeout and classifies the rendering as partial at build().

code_changes.fixed_code:
# In DocxRenderer.render: hand the lazily imported library's cell class to the writer.
        writer = _Writer(builder, _Notes(document), docx.table._Cell)

# In _Writer:
    def __init__(self, builder: Builder, notes: _Notes, cell: Any) -> None:
        self._builder = builder
        self._notes = notes
        self._cell = cell
        self._pictures = 0

    def table(self, table: Any) -> None:
        grid = max(1, len(table._tbl.tblGrid.gridCol_lst))
        rows: list[list[str]] = []
        for tr in table._tbl.tr_lst:
            if rows and self._builder.out_of_time():
                break
            above = rows[-1] if rows else []
            cells: list[str] = []
            for tc in tr.tc_lst:
                if len(cells) >= grid:
                    break
                at = len(cells)
                if tc.vMerge == "continue":
                    text = above[at] if at < len(above) else ""
                else:
                    text = self._cell(tc, table).text
                cells.extend([text] * max(1, min(tc.grid_span, grid - at)))
            rows.append(cells)
        self._builder.table(rows)

likelihood.reason: Any principal with write rights can plant the payload; it is trivial and a few KB. It needs the docx extra installed and fires only when the operator runs reindex, which is routine maintenance.

impact.reason: Memory and CPU on the operator's reindex grow linearly with an attribute value up to 2^31-1. They run in the in-process offload pool shared with every agent's grep, and that work cannot be interrupted. Observed: 473 MiB and 22 s at 1e6. Extrapolated, not executed: process-wide OOM or hours-long stalls at the maximum, and an un-landed row that is retried on every reindex. This is availability only; no data is disclosed or changed.

confidence.reason: The source path is verified line by line. The library behaviour was read from the installed python-docx 1.2.0, and linear growth at constant input size was reproduced in the approved sandbox with counted calls. Only the maximum-span process exhaustion is extrapolated, not observed. An independent Phase 5 rerun reproduced the linear growth, and the corrected fix was executed against both the attack input and a merged-cell table.
